title: The Fisheries Integrated Modeling System is a generalized stock assessment platform built using good software practices
content:
Abstract
As scientists adopt computing advances, there is a need to develop a flexible computing framework for the assessment of marine resources. We envision a new collection of software tools for stock assessment, the Fisheries Integrated Modeling System (FIMS), that standardizes modeling approaches and provides a clear pathway to onboard new good practices. Increasing consistency among assessments reduces maintenance costs, standardizes implementation and adoption of best practices, and increases communication. When designing and developing a new system, a collaborative, bottom-up approach to model development yields improved code and a larger pool of collaborators contributing to and improving the modeling approach. Desired features for FIMS were collated by pooling regional requirements, followed by national prioritization to drive development priorities. FIMS benefits from a diverse set of contributors who gather requirements, write code, set up tests and case studies, implement automated tests, write documentation, and provide outreach to the fisheries science community. A major success of the FIMS effort has been improved testing using both automated tests and case studies that allow collaborators to identify issues and missing features early and often within the development process. A modular architecture yields streamlined incorporation of new good practices but at the cost of a steep learning curve for new developers to understand the code base. The collaborative approach to FIMS allows the development team to respond to this, and other issues that arise, and adjust the development process accordingly. FIMS is designed to meet the needs of many stock assessment users who prefer choosing from within preexisting, well-tested feature sets and to evolve over time as new science and good practices become available.
